title: Code Review, Formatting, and Static Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of code review, formatting, and static analysis using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates code review, formatting, and static analysis.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Code Review, Formatting, and Static Analysis** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Kotlin Coding Conventions, Linters and Formatting Tools, Reviewing Changes and Enforcing Standards—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Code Review, Formatting, and Static Analysis removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates code review, formatting, and static analysis. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving kotlin coding conventions.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain code review, formatting, and static analysis without copying the lesson wording.
